The Vice President / Chief Technology Officer (VP/CTO) is an executive leadership role responsible for the organization’s enterprise technology strategy, architecture, infrastructure, and operations, enabling Premier Health’s digital health transformation ambitions. Reporting to the Chief Digital Information Officer (CDIO), this individual identifies key emerging trends and technologies, evolves the architecture to support new and emerging technologies, modernizes the infrastructure, and ensures the reliable, secure, and efficient operation of all technology platforms and services supporting business, clinical, and operational objectives.

The VP/CTO acts as both a technology visionary and an operational leader, balancing long-term digital transformation initiatives with day-to-day technology service delivery. This individual provides leadership to enterprise architects, senior product managers, technology specialists, and professionals across Technology Infrastructure, Technology Operations Management, and IT Service Management (ITSM). As a member of the Senior Digital Health and Technology Leadership team, the VP/CTO drives technology innovation, transformation, and technical operations; leads Agile/DevOps teams; leads cloud transformation; and partners with clinical, business, and informatics leaders to ensure technology solutions meet end-user needs and support a modern, patient-centered, high-performing health system.

Scope/Span Of Control

Enterprise-wide accountability for technology strategy, architecture, infrastructure, technology operations, service desk/desktop support, and IT service management across all Premier Health facilities and lines of business. Key areas of responsibility include but are not limited to: multi-site technology operations, hosting (including data center, co-location and cloud), all LAN and WAN network services, server and storge strategy and operations, desktop engineering and service delivery, service desk operations and IT Service Management (ITSM) standards and strategy for the department.

Education

Minimum Level of Education Required:
Bachelor’s degree

Type of Degree:
Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Arts

Area of Study or Major:
Health Care Administration, Business, Information Systems, Computer Science, Industrial Engineering, Computer Science Management, or a related engineering/technical discipline

Preferred Educational Qualifications:
Master’s degree (MBA, MHA, MIS, or related field)

Position Specific Testing Requirement:
N/A

Licensure/Certification/Registration

None required. Preferred: ITIL, PMP, Lean Six Sigma/Organizational Change Management (OCM), or relevant technical certifications (e.g., cloud, cybersecurity, network).

Experience

10+ years of progressive technology leadership experience, including at least 5 years in a senior IT leadership role

Prior Job Title or Occupational Experience:
Technology Management, CIO, CTO, VP or Director of Technology/Infrastructure

Prior Specific Functional Responsibilities:
Innovation, Entrepreneurship, Operations Leadership, IT Leadership, Digital Leadership, Infrastructure/Technology Operations Management, Service Desk/Desktop Support, IT Service Management (ITSM)

Preferred Experience:
Healthcare or hospital/ambulatory experience; Digital Leadership or IT Leadership; leading multi-site technology operations, service desk, and desktop support teams across a distributed facility footprint

Other Experience Requirements:
Proven leadership of successful transformation initiatives; deep experience managing enterprise infrastructure and disaster recovery programs, and partnering closely with cybersecurity/security leadership on secure technology operations; experience standing up or maturing an IT Service Management (ITSM) practice and associated tooling; understanding of core business and clinical processes and their associated technology solutions; strong written and verbal communication and executive presentation skills; change management; Lean or Six Sigma experience; vendor contract negotiation; and critical problem-solving and design

Knowledge/Skills

Understands the business and technical impact of emerging technologies and the issues involved in their adoption; no longer needs to be a hands-on practitioner.
Strong business acumen, customer experience, communication, and relationship-building skills.
Strategic and architectural thinker able to translate business and clinical objectives into actionable technology plans.
Strong architectural understanding of compute and compute hosting strategies, data center management, networking, service desk leadership, and desktop engineering and support.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Slack is looking for an Engineering Manager on the Core Services engineering team. The purpose of this role is to keep Slack working seamlessly at massive scale — it's the infrastructure that keeps Slack feeling lightning fast. This person will be a steward of some of the most critical, high-throughput systems at Slack — the kind of work where doing it well means millions of users, at the world’s most important and interesting companies, never experience a hiccup.

About The Opportunity

We operate at tremendous scale with systems that process millions of events per second. Our team maintains and builds performant services that include:

Edge Caches
Realtime Services
Enterprise Key Management (EKM)
International Data Residency (IDR)
Image Uploads, Downloads, and Proxying

We've done our job correctly when none of our users think about us, much like a vital utility. Slack's backend services are written in Go and Java, and Slack's API is built on PHP/Hack.

The Core Services Team

We are a team building critical services that enable Slack to scale for our largest customers. Our edge caches power the most latency-critical queries for our largest entities today, serving approximately 35% of all Slack API traffic. Our Realtime Services (RTS) power Slack's core messaging stack — running 10 services, 4 of which are mission-critical Tier 0 services — ensuring that messages, presence, and real-time events are delivered reliably at scale. We also own services that power Slack's Enterprise Key Management and International Data Residency features, enabling Slack to win and retain enterprise and government customers with strict compliance requirements (FedRAMP/NIST).

We have a strong commitment to quality and understand that simplicity and reliability are the foundations of our work.

We are actively building the future of edge services at Slack, so we can support a growing number of globally distributed customers with their compliance requirements with minimal latency.

What You'll Be Doing:

Owning the technical direction and roadmap across the Core Services portfolio: Edge Caches, Realtime Services, Enterprise Key Management, International Data Residency, and Image Proxying and Uploads. You’ll have large footprint and the opportunity to drive major impact. And you'll decide what to invest in now, what to sequence later, and what to decline — balancing reliability, migration, and new capability work.
Leading a multi-system migration of Flannel to Loom, our next-generation edge cache, while keeping the current systems running at full reliability for millions of users. You'll drive the team to ship new capabilities without introducing risk to infrastructure that people depend on daily.
Driving delivery and execution while maintaining reliability as a top priority, including sprint planning, product launches, incident follow-ups, operational sustainability analyses, and building the technical case for investment with leadership. You'll ensure the team doesn't trade reliability for velocity, but is always high-performing.
Owning on-call operations and incident management for Tier 0 services. You'll manage on-call rotations across partnering teams, triage production issues, lead incident response for your services, and drive improvements to runbooks, alerting, and operational tooling.
Partnering cross-functionally with Product, Sales, Compliance, Security, AWS, and other infrastructure teams on dependencies, timelines, and risks. You'll be the shortest path to solutions — whether it's unblocking a compliance audit for South Korea, coordinating IDR region launches with Sales and AWS, or negotiating priorities with partner teams for shared work.
Representing your team's work in leadership reviews, quarterly and annual planning, and executive forums. You'll build compelling business-and-technical cases for your team's investments and tell your leadership what's really going on early enough that nothing becomes a fire drill.
Building and maintaining a high-trust team culture where engineers do impactful work and grow. You'll hire well, manage performance with fairness and transparency, mentor emerging technical leaders, and celebrate your team's wins.
Managing cost and capacity for services that run at massive scale, working with finance on AWS spend trends, exec-approved budget increases, and cost-saving initiatives like the Loom migration (projected $1-2M savings).
Driving the team to adopt AI development tooling for maximum impact, while maintaining engineering rigor and quality for critical infrastructure.

You're Our Person If:

You've led engineering teams for 5+ years building and operating high-scale, high-availability backend infrastructure or distributed systems.
You have strong software engineering fundamentals with previous experience as a Senior+ backend engineer, with enough depth to be credible in architecture discussions about caching, distributed systems, observability and reliability best practices, and system design — and to build SME knowledge in a new area fast.
You have a history of managing Tier 0 / Tier 1 services where uptime matters deeply, including owning on-call rotations, leading incident response, and driving operational improvements.
You have experience with realtime messaging systems or event-driven architectures at scale — presence, message delivery, pub/sub, or similar systems where latency and reliability directly impact user experience.
You have experience leading multi-quarter migration or platform evolution projects while simultaneously keeping existing systems reliable.
You've managed teams through prioritization trade-offs — weighing reliability vs. feature work vs. cost vs. compliance — and can articulate those decisions to both engineers and executives.
You have experience partnering with cross-functional stakeholders (Product, Sales, Compliance, Security, Infrastructure) to turn business requirements into engineering plans.
You understand how to build a high-performing team culture: hiring, performance management, retention of top performers, and growing new technical leaders.
You have experience managing engineers across multiple time zones, with an async rhythm that doesn't depend on overlap hours.
An understanding of how and where AI software development tooling can be deployed for maximum team impact.

Even Better If:

You have experience with the Go and/or Java programming language at scale.
Experience with AWS infrastructure, including multi-region architectures.
Experience with Kubernetes and container-based deployments.
Experience working within highly regulated environments where an understanding of FedRAMP/NIST frameworks was essential.
Experience with Enterprise Key Management, data residency, or compliance-driven infrastructure.
You've managed teams responsible for Edge Caching, CDN, or API gateway systems.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Data Engineering
jobs.description:
JLL Technologies is a specialized group within JLL. At JLL Technologies, our mission is to bring technological innovation to commercial real estate. We deliver unparalleled digital advisory, implementation, and services solutions to organizations globally. Our goal is to leverage technology to increase the value and liquidity of the world’s buildings, while enhancing the productivity and happiness of those that occupy them.

The Data Engineering team builds and operates the data products and pipelines that power JLL’s Corporate Functions, including areas such as finance, HR, Legal, Compliance and shared services. Working on the Enterprise Data Platform (EDP), we turn internal enterprise data into trusted, governed, and increasingly real-time assets that leaders and teams across the firm rely on for reporting, planning, and operational decisions.

What this job involves

As Senior Data Engineering Manager, you will lead multiple related scrum teams of data engineers responsible for Corporate Functions data – from ingestion and streaming pipelines through curated, governed data products. Your teams own the reliability, quality, and timeliness of the data that underpins enterprise reporting, financial and workforce analytics, and shared-services operations.

You will own delivery and direction for the Corporate Functions data engineering function: setting priorities across teams, allocating resources, guiding technical design, and partnering with product, analytics, and business leaders to translate needs into a clear roadmap. You will be accountable for team outcomes, data quality standards, and the continuous improvement of engineering practices.

The ideal candidate blends the technical credibility of a Lead Data Engineer – hands-on depth in Python, Azure, and streaming architectures – with proven people leadership, and the ability to build trust with senior business stakeholders.

What you’ll get to do

As Senior Data Engineering Manager, your “customers” include leaders and teams in Finance, HR, Legal, Compliance and other Corporate Functions, data analysts and BI teams, product managers, and fellow platform and governance teams across JLL Technologies. Your mission is to lead the Corporate Functions data engineering function – defining the roadmap, operating model, and quality standards that make data trusted, timely, and reusable.

This is an opportunity to shape how streaming and governed data enable faster, better-informed decisions across the enterprise – and to grow a high-performing engineering organization while doing it.

Key responsibilities

Technical Leadership:
Provide hands-on technical direction for batch and streaming data pipelines built on Azure, Python, and Spark. Guide architecture and design reviews, set engineering standards for reusable frameworks, and stay close to critical technical risks.

Real-Time and Streaming Data Delivery:
Lead the design and operation of event-driven pipelines using technologies such as Kafka and Spark Streaming, so that financial, workforce, and operational data reaches downstream consumers with the latency and reliability the business requires.

Data Governance and Quality:
Own data quality, lineage, cataloging, and stewardship practices for Corporate Functions data domains, including sensitive finance and HR data. Define measurable quality standards, automate validation and monitoring in pipelines, and partner with enterprise governance and security teams to ensure compliance with JLL data policies and access controls.

Delivery Management:
Set priorities and manage execution across multiple scrum teams. Balance roadmap commitments, technical debt, and operational demands; maintain predictable delivery; and adapt plans as business needs evolve.

Platform Alignment and Modernization:
Align team deliverables with the Enterprise Data Platform strategy. Drive adoption of platform standards, ingestion patterns, and cloud-native services, and contribute to modernization of legacy data assets.

Reliability and Operational Excellence:
Establish CI/CD, observability, and incident management practices that keep pipelines healthy. Ensure teams meet service-level expectations and learn from production issues through blameless reviews.

Cross-Functional Leadership:
Collaborate with product, analytics, data science, platform, security, and governance teams to deliver end-to-end data solutions. Resolve dependencies, negotiate shared priorities, and keep teams aligned on outcomes.

Team Development and Mentorship:
Recruit, coach, and retain strong engineers and team leads. Set clear expectations, provide regular feedback, build career growth paths, and foster a culture of inclusion, ownership, and continuous learning.

Stakeholder Management:
Build trusted relationships with Corporate Functions business and technology leaders. Communicate status, risks, and trade-offs clearly, manage expectations on scope and timelines, and ensure engineering work maps to business value.

Resource and Budget Planning:
Partner with leadership on headcount, vendor, and cloud cost planning for your teams, optimizing talent utilization and cost efficiency across products and initiatives.

Who you are

You are a people-first engineering leader who has grown from strong hands-on data engineering roots. You earn credibility with engineers by understanding the technical detail – from distributed processing to data modeling trade-offs – while inspiring them through clear direction, coaching, and high standards. You navigate competing priorities with composure, explain complex topics plainly to executives, and hold yourself accountable for both team outcomes and the quality of the data your teams deliver. You are energized by turning ambiguous business needs into reliable, governed data products.

Required Qualifications

People management: 2+ years directly managing data engineers or technical individual contributors; experience setting priorities, allocating work, and coaching teams; managing managers is not required.
Data engineering experience: 7+ years in data engineering, including multiple large and complex projects delivered end to end.
Technical depth: Advanced Python and SQL; strong experience with Azure data services and distributed processing (e.g., Spark/PySpark); experience building reusable frameworks.
Streaming: Hands-on experience designing or leading real-time data pipelines with Kafka, Spark Streaming, or equivalent technologies.
Data governance and quality: Working knowledge of data quality frameworks, lineage, metadata management, and data governance practices.
Delivery: Experience managing or training teams of data engineers and setting priorities across multiple data engineering workstreams in an agile environment.
Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage both technical and business stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
Experience with corporate data domains such as finance, HR, or shared services (e.g., ERP, HRIS, or enterprise reporting data), or in commercial real estate.
Experience with NoSQL, graph, or multi-model databases (e.g., CosmosDB, MongoDB) and complex cross-system integrations.
Familiarity with data cataloging and governance tooling, and with CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code practices.
Experience with modern lakehouse or data platform architectures and enterprise data platforms.
Exposure to applying AI/ML or LLM-based capabilities to data engineering and data quality workflows.

Key attributes

Leadership:
Builds and retains strong teams; delegates effectively while staying close to critical technical risks.

Stakeholder Partnership:

The Director of Broadcast Engineering leads the reliability, development, and daily upkeep of technical systems and engineering support for the control room and connected production infrastructure at Barclays Center. jobs.title: VP / Director of Engineering
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Expand Power is building solid-state transformers and modular power electronics for a decentralized, decentralized, resilient grid. We're a small team doing hard, meaningful engineering, and we're just getting started.

We’re backed by several Department of Energy programs, Berkeley National Laboratory, the Activate Fellowship, and world-class pre-seed investors and VCs. Our advisory network includes prominent leaders in power electronics, high frequency magnetics, the electric utility industry, and deep tech commercialization.

Why This Role Exists

We’re at a critical inflection point in the grid, where we have new sources and loads at a capacity that we couldn’t have dreamed of. Traditional grid electronics, with their lack of control and DC based capabilities, just can’t keep up. With real customer demand, we’re closing the gap between the grid of today and the grid of the future by building innovative smart transformers and modular power electronics. We’re excited to commercialize and deploy our technology across multiple customers for real world impact. We are growing the team and are looking for passionate, dedicated, ambitious hires who are excited by ownership and the electrification of our grid.

The Vice President / Director of Engineering will serve as a founding team member and strategic partner to the CEO, leading the architecture of Expand’s technical stack and defining the next generation of power electronics for the grid. As a core member of the founding leadership team, the VP will shape Expand’s technical priorities through immediate pilots and deployment, ensuring customers receive a high performance, reliable, product. 

This role is critical to Expand’s success– you will be working closely with the founding team and in the field with real customers, reporting to the CEO. In this role, you’ll set technical requirements and ensure customer functionality is translated into complex technical goals. You’ll be deeply hands-on and in the weeds while also leading the technology roadmap and progress. You will guide technical development of our proprietary power electronics technology for immediate deployment while interfacing with customers. You will have a critical role in shaping the core technology, product direction, and culture of a cross-functional and rapidly growing early stage company. You’ll be one of the most valuable founding members of a company shaping the future of the electric grid. In doing so, you will push the limits of what’s achievable with high-frequency power electronics and grid modernization

Your Day to Day and Key Responsibilities

You will be leading Expand’s technical strategy from customer discussions to prototype to certifications to manufacturing while guiding the engineering team and contributing to technical designs. You’ll use creativity and innovation to:

Leadership
Leverage deep expertise in power electronics to understand complex customer needs, set and lead the technical roadmap, and execute while adhering to regulatory requirements
Lead the development and evolution of Expand’s technical stack, aligning customer demand, industry trends, and operational capabilities in direct partnership with the CEO
Act as the technical point of contact for customers, translating requirements into engineering tasks
Define and oversee operational excellence for Expand’s technical spaces, ensuring a safe, high-quality, and consistent user experience
Lead and scale the technical team, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement
Support business development efforts to bring new customers
Provide strategic technical insight to inform Expand’s broader growth, partnership, and capital planning decisions
Architect the technical narratives for capital formation efforts alongside the CEO, including input for grants, funding, and early commercial partnerships
Contribute as a core member of the founding team to define and institutionalize Expand’s mission, values, safety standards, and internal operating systems
Represent Expand in select industry, government, and customer-facing forums
Maintain alignment of technical standards and customer experience
Partner with the CEO to forecast hiring needs aligned with customer demand and program growth

Hands on Engineering
Lead the development of power conversion systems from first principles to deployment for manufacturability and flexibility 
Document technical specifications, architecture decisions, and validation reports
Lead IP generation process
Simulate, model, and design circuits and converters to maximize performance and reliability, as needed

What You’ve Done

Required Experience
You have deep power electronics expertise, with a proven ability to scale a product from inception to manufacturing while building a powerful team. You’ve done this before: you are a highly experienced electrical engineering leader, a master of your craft. Guiding hardware development is your bread and butter, but it still gives you excitement and fulfillment, especially with a mission you care deeply about. You have a proven track record of driving and implementing innovation and R&D for commercialization. 

You also have experience in
Leadership in power electronics and hardware design with demonstrated experience advancing new technologies and products toward manufacturing 
Building multi-disciplinary power electronics teams
Architecting multi-year technical roadmaps aligned with commercialization timelines, customer demand, and operational capabilities in a founding-stage, high-growth, or innovation-driven organization
Bringing a product to market while meeting certification standards and regulations
Technical consulting or customer-facing roles, with the ability to translate ambiguous research goals into precise commercialization steps
Strong relationship building and communication skills, with the ability to build trust across technical teams, customers, and senior stakeholders ranging from academic researchers to industry experts
Startups or fast-paced, early stage company environments
High frequency and high power converters, including modular multilevel converters, resonant converters, or MVDC distribution
Fluency in Altium and/or KiCad, ANSYS, Spice, PLECS, PSIM

Bonus Experience
Medium voltage power electronics and operation
Planar magnetics
DERs and/or inverter product development
Knowledge of relevant industry standards (UL 1741, etc)
Overseeing or operating technical laboratory, prototyping, or shared infrastructure environments with rigorous attention to safety (EH&S), resource allocation, and operational efficiency

You’re described as a
Fast moving, hands-on builder, taking responsibility for outcomes from design through deployment and hungry for ownership
Independent, gritty problem solver, who thrives in uncertainty, loves a challenge, and responds to obstacles with the best of their abilities
Strong and collaborative communicator, able to explain technical decisions to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders, and to share feedback openly and kindly
Mission-driven, motivated by positive real-world impact and passionate about pushing the boundaries of power electronics and electrification
Fearless and endlessly curious, energized by open questions and new possibilities, willing to bet on bold ideas and learn fast from what the hardware tells you, and taking intelligent risks with a sense of wonder and a drive to explore what's possible

Don't meet every requirement? Apply anyway—we value diverse backgrounds and potential over perfect checklists. We're more interested in what you can do than in every box being ticked.

How We Work & Compensation

Come work on breakthrough technology in a collaborative, mission-driven culture with direct influence over company trajectory and room to grow as the team scales. This is an onsite position based in the San Francisco Bay Area. Minimum travel will be expected. We are open to supporting relocation for the right candidate.

We want you to stay for a while– you will receive $175,000 - $225,000 base with meaningful early employee equity, based on level and experience, as well as benefits:

jobs.description:
Career-defining. Life-changing.

At iRhythm, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your skills and your career while impacting the lives of people around the world. iRhythm is shaping a future where everyone, everywhere can access the best possible cardiac health solutions. Every day, we collaborate, create, and constantly reimagine what’s possible. We think big and move fast, driven by our commitment to put patients first and improve lives. We need builders like you. Curious and innovative problem solvers looking for the chance to meaningfully shape the future of cardiac health, our company, and your career

About This Role

iRhythm is seeking a Vice President of Software Engineering to provide technical and organizational leadership across our regulated software platforms. Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Systems Development, this leader is accountable for ensuring the successful delivery, performance, and scalability of software products and platforms. These solutions enable clinician workflows, enhance patient experiences, integrate connected medical devices, and provide the data infrastructure necessary to support innovation, operational excellence, and growth. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution at scale, requiring executive leadership and offering exceptional visibility across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Software Delivery & Operational Execution

Lead end-to-end software engineering execution across clinical, patient-facing, platform, and device-integrated software systems within a highly regulated Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) environment.
Establish and continuously evolve the engineering operating systems, governance frameworks, and development practices that enable disciplined planning, transparent execution, effective risk management, and predictable delivery across a complex software portfolio.
Champion continuous improvement initiatives that measurably enhance engineering velocity, product quality, release confidence, system reliability, and customer outcomes.
Ensure software development lifecycle processes consistently meet regulatory, compliance, and quality standards, including FDA, IEC 62304, ISO 13485, cybersecurity, and internal Quality Management System (QMS) requirements.
Translate complex technical concepts, delivery risks, and strategic tradeoffs into clear, actionable insights for executive leadership and key stakeholders.
Advance software engineering capabilities through scalable CI/CD frameworks, development platforms, automation, and engineering enablement tools appropriate for regulated medical technology environments.
Lead the responsible adoption and governance of AI-assisted software development practices to accelerate innovation, enhance productivity, improve quality, and reduce delivery risk.
Establish a metrics-driven engineering culture by leveraging meaningful operational and quality indicators to increase transparency, predictability, accountability, and data-informed decision making.

Team Development & Leadership

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing organization of software engineering directors, managers, and senior technical leaders, fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and execution excellence.
Serve as a thought leader, trusted advisor and mentor to engineering leaders, cultivating leadership capability, organizational resilience, and a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and technical excellence across the company.

Cross-Functional & Strategic Contributions

Partner closely with executive and functional leaders across Product Security, Software Quality, Research & Systems Engineering, Machine Learning, and IT to ensure seamless execution, architectural alignment, and delivery excellence across the product portfolio.
Drive alignment and shared accountability across Product Management, Clinical, Quality, Regulatory, and other cross-functional teams to successfully deliver innovative solutions from concept through commercialization.
Lead software engineering diligence, technical assessments, and post-acquisition integration activities in support of the company's mergers and acquisitions strategy.
Contribute to the development and execution of the long-term software platform, architecture, and technology strategy, ensuring scalability, innovation, and competitive differentiation.

Qualifications

Required Experience

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
10+ years of progressive software engineering leadership experience, including leadership of large-scale engineering organizations and senior technology leaders.
Demonstrated success leading the development and delivery of Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) solutions within highly regulated medical device environments.
Proven track record bringing complex regulated software products from concept and development through verification, validation, regulatory approval, commercialization, and post-market support.
Deep expertise in FDA software regulations, IEC 62304, ISO 13485, and medical device quality systems, with a strong understanding of applying these requirements within modern software development environments.
Experience leading complex, matrixed software engineering organizations through periods of growth, transformation, organizational change, and technology modernization.

Preferred Experience

Experience spanning both high-growth and established healthcare, medical device, digital health, or regulated technology organizations.
Experience scaling software organizations supporting connected products, cloud platforms, data ecosystems, and customer-facing applications.
Exposure to technical diligence, integration planning, or software leadership support for mergers and acquisitions.
Demonstrated success modernizing software delivery capabilities, including CI/CD frameworks, automation, and engineering productivity tools within regulated environments.
Practical experience evaluating, implementing, and governing AI-assisted software development practices to improve engineering effectiveness, product quality, and delivery outcomes.

Leadership Profile

Strategic and execution-oriented leader with the ability to translate business priorities into operational excellence and measurable outcomes.
Equally comfortable shaping long-term technology strategy and engaging directly in delivery execution, organizational design, and engineering operations.
Proven builder of high-performing teams and leadership talent, with a strong track record of developing leaders and creating a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Exceptional cross-functional collaborator capable of influencing executive stakeholders and aligning diverse teams around shared objectives.
Data-driven, pragmatic, and decisive, with the ability to balance speed, quality, regulatory compliance, and business impact.
Resilient and adaptable leader who thrives in complex environments and successfully leads organizations through change, growth, and transformation.

jobs.title: Head of Engineering
jobs.description:
Head of Engineering — Autonomous Fleet Platform

Build the software operating layer for autonomous mobility

San Francisco Bay Area, CA

Location:
Downtown San Francisco / Bay Area — in person when required
Type:
Full-Time
Industry:
Autonomous Mobility | Fleet Software | AI Infrastructure | EV & AV Operations
Website:
https://autzu.com/
About Autzu

Autzu is building the software and operational layer that autonomous mobility will run on.
Over the past several years, Autzu has developed and operated technology supporting live electric-vehicle fleets across the U.S. and Canada. We are now evolving that experience into an autonomous-ready platform capable of deploying, monitoring, coordinating, and managing vehicles across multiple operators, vehicle platforms, and markets.
Our mission is to make autonomous fleets commercially deployable at scale.
Autzu will own the software layer connecting:
Autonomous vehicles and fleet operators
Vehicle state, telemetry, diagnostics, and readiness
Dispatch, scheduling, charging, maintenance, and service workflows
Remote operations and human-in-the-loop support
Data infrastructure, operational intelligence, and AI-driven automation
Future autonomous hubs and robotic servicing systems

We are not building another autonomous-driving stack. We are building the platform that allows different autonomous systems to operate reliably across real-world fleets and markets.
Autzu will also work directly with Infra
, a separately structured robotics-infrastructure company focused on physical autonomous hubs and robotic servicing systems. Autzu’s platform will provide the software, data, orchestration, and integration layer connecting autonomous vehicles with Infra’s physical infrastructure.
The Opportunity

We are seeking a hands-on, execution-focused Head of Engineering
to lead Autzu’s software organization through its next stage of development.
This is a founding engineering leadership seat for Autzu’s autonomous-systems platform.
The role is not focused on building robotic arms or developing an autonomous-driving stack. It is focused on building the software platform that connects vehicles, operators, partners, operational teams, and future robotic infrastructure.
You will own and strengthen Autzu’s existing fleet platform while architecting its evolution into a secure, scalable, multi-operator autonomous fleet orchestration system.
You must be comfortable maintaining live production software while modernizing the architecture and developing new autonomous-vehicle capabilities in parallel.
You Will

Own and strengthen Autzu’s existing fleet and operations platform.
Define the architecture and technical roadmap for Autzu’s autonomous fleet platform.
Build an agnostic integration layer capable of supporting multiple autonomous-vehicle operators, OEMs, and technology stacks.
Lead the development of vehicle-state, telemetry, diagnostics, readiness, dispatch, and operational workflow systems.
Develop the software interfaces connecting Autzu’s platform with Infra’s future robotics and autonomous-hub infrastructure.
Improve platform reliability, data integrity, security, and system observability.
Reduce technical debt without disrupting live operations.
Hire and lead a lean, senior engineering team across backend systems, autonomous systems, data, AI, and edge or IoT integration.
Work directly with Autzu’s founder, executive team, board, customers, and strategic technology partners.
Represent Autzu’s technical architecture and product direction in partner, investor, and fundraising conversations.

Core Mandate

Keep Autzu’s current fleet software operating reliably while transforming it into a modular, secure, autonomous-ready platform capable of coordinating vehicles and operations across multiple cities, countries, vehicle types, and autonomy providers.
This includes:
Stabilizing uptime, data quality, and operational reliability.
Introducing clear service boundaries, APIs, and data contracts without a disruptive rewrite.
Creating a common vehicle and fleet data model across multiple platforms.
Building real-time vehicle-state, telemetry, diagnostics, and exception-management systems.
Developing integration frameworks for AV operators, OEMs, mobility platforms, telematics providers, charging networks, and maintenance partners.
Establishing a software interface between Autzu’s fleet platform and Infra’s robotic hub systems.
Strengthening CI/CD, automated testing, release management, incident response, audit logging, and on-call processes.
Building the migration path from today’s fleet platform into a multi-city autonomous operations layer.
Introducing AI agents and automation where they improve reliability, efficiency, and operational decision-making.

What You’ll Do

Define and own Autzu’s engineering vision and roadmap alongside the founder and executive team.
Lead backend, cloud, data, platform, and selected edge or embedded-software functions.
Make key architecture decisions while remaining close enough to the implementation to review designs, challenge assumptions, and guide senior engineers.
Build systems for vehicle onboarding, state management, fleet readiness, dispatch, monitoring, diagnostics, and operational workflows.
Develop real-time APIs and event-driven integrations across autonomous vehicles, fleet operators, and external services.
Build the systems needed for remote supervision, exception handling, human intervention, and operational escalation.
Oversee integrations with marketplace APIs, payments, telematics, charging networks, maintenance providers, identity systems, and compliance reporting.
Develop data and AI systems that identify operational issues, automate repetitive workflows, and improve fleet utilization.
Establish engineering standards across architecture, code quality, testing, security, observability, and release management.
Manage existing contractors while recruiting and developing key internal engineering leaders.
Create a builder culture grounded in accountability, speed, technical rigor, and measurable operational outcomes.

Must-Have Experience

8+ years of software or systems engineering experience.
4+ years in engineering leadership as a Head of Engineering, Director, VP Engineering, CTO, Engineering Manager, or comparable technical leader.
Proven ownership of a live production software platform supporting operationally critical workflows.
Experience building distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, APIs, data pipelines, and complex third-party integrations.
Demonstrated ability to modernize architecture and reduce technical debt while continuing to ship new capabilities.
Strong operational discipline around uptime, observability, incident response, release cycles, security, and data integrity.
Experience hiring and leading strong engineers in a fast-moving or resource-constrained environment.
Ability to translate business and operational requirements into scalable technical systems.
Comfortable working directly with external technical partners, customers, executives, and investors.
Hands-on enough to lead architecture reviews, evaluate code and system design, and guide Staff or Principal-level engineers.

Strongly Preferred

Experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics software, mobility, rideshare, logistics, fleet management, connected vehicles, or intelligent transportation.
Experience with fleet orchestration, remote operations, vehicle telemetry, diagnostics, mapping, calibration, simulation, or autonomous-system infrastructure.
Familiarity with edge computing, embedded systems, IoT, telematics, CAN or vehicle interfaces.
Experience integrating software platforms with physical hardware or robotics systems.
Familiarity with NVIDIA’s automotive, edge-computing, simulation, or Physical AI ecosystem.
Experience building AI agents, operational automation, predictive systems, or intelligent decision-support tools.
Experience with safety-critical, regulated, or compliance-heavy environments.
Experience scaling software platforms across multiple cities, countries, or operating partners.

What We Offer

A founding engineering leadership role in Autzu’s transition into autonomous fleet operations.
Significant ownership over the engineering strategy, architecture, team, and technical roadmap.
Competitive compensation, performance incentives, and meaningful equity.
A dedicated budget to build a lean, high-caliber engineering organization.
Direct partnership with the founder, executive team, board, and strategic technology partners.
The opportunity to build the software platform connecting autonomous vehicles, fleet operations, and future robotic infrastructure.
A direct working relationship with Infra as its physical robotics and autonomous-hub systems are developed.
The opportunity to grow into broader technology leadership as Autzu’s platform, team, and international operations scale.

Why This Role Matters

Autonomous vehicles cannot scale through driving technology alone.
They require software that understands where every vehicle is, what condition it is in, what it needs next, when human intervention is required, and how it moves through charging, maintenance, service, and deployment workflows.
Autzu is building that operating layer.
The Head of Engineering will be responsible for turning that vision into a reliable production platform.

jobs.description:
Description

Technology Director — Global Health

ICF's Global Health and Development (GHD) line of business, part of the Health, People, and Human Services (HPHS) Group, is seeking a Technology Director
to lead technology modernization efforts across various global health and survey programs. This is a hands-on leadership role. You will own delivery of the program's technology work from end to end. You will also serve as one of its technical leads and architects, designing systems yourself as well as directing the team that builds them. You will bridge ICF's applied AI and software engineers with its survey methodologists, statisticians, field operations staff, and country partners. You will be accountable to the funder for results, including the decision to redirect work that isn't performing and move the funding to work that is.

This position can be remote within the United States, with occasional international travel.

It is contingent upon award of program funding.

Key Responsibilities

Technology Modernization Delivery Leadership

Own delivery of the program's AI innovation portfolio. The workstreams cover automated data-to-report production, natural-language data access, multilingual questionnaire design, field data quality, and new measurement approaches.
Run the stage-gate process. Lead go/no-go reviews, and make and defend decisions to stop workstreams, publish what they learned, and reallocate their funding.
Serve as the principal technical counterpart to the funder. Lead progress reporting and learning reviews. Communicate results candidly, including negative ones.
Manage the innovation portfolio, schedule, and risks with the project manager, including inference and cloud operating costs.
Coordinate across global development programs. Share successes, failures, and methods with technology partners to avoid duplicating work.

Technical Leadership & Architecture

Act as technical lead and architect for a cluster of workstreams. Own their system design, write the design documents, and stay hands-on through prototyping and production.
Define acceptance criteria before the work is judged. With survey experts, set the quantitative quality thresholds each tool must meet, and hold the team (and yourself) to them.
Set architecture and standards across the portfolio: model selection and routing, privacy-preserving design, offline and low-connectivity deployment, and security.
Set engineering practice for the team, including specification-driven development with agentic coding tools, evaluation-first delivery, code review, and testing.
Protect data quality and comparability. Work with survey methodologists so that no innovation breaks the comparability of data across countries and over time.
Oversee responsible AI, data governance, and ethics. Make sure the program meets ICF security standards, IRB requirements, and partner-country data sovereignty expectations.

Team Leadership & Collaboration

Lead and mentor the program's technology team, including applied AI, software, ML, and platform engineers.
Bridge technology and survey expertise. Make sure survey methodologists, statisticians, and field teams shape what gets built, and that engineers understand how surveys work.
Work with national statistical offices and ministries of health, together with ICF's country engagement leads, to design tools that countries want and can run on their own.
Share the program's results openly through public documentation, publications, and presentations at technical and global health conferences.
Contribute to business growth efforts including proactive engagement with potential clients, preparation of white papers, and proposal development.

Minimum Required Experience

Bachelors degree in IT, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field (or equivalent experience)
Minimum 10 years of professional experience designing and delivering technology solutions, including hands-on architecture of multiple complex systems taken into production
Minimum 5 years leading and mentoring software or data engineering teams to build products or deploy systems

Additional Required Skills And Experience

A track record of architecting and delivering AI/ML or LLM-powered systems in production, and the ability to explain how their quality was measured and where they failed
Experience leading a multi-workstream technology program for a foundation, donor, or government client, with accountability for budget and results
Deep knowledge of system architecture, data pipelines, software development methods, and at least one major cloud platform (e.g., AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud)
Hands-on familiarity with agentic coding tools and specification-driven development, and experience setting how a team uses them
U.S. citizenship is required by federal government contract

Preferred Skills

Working proficiency in French or Portuguese
Background in survey operations or data collection, such as work on or with the Demographic & Health Surveys (DHS) Program, Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS), Living Standards Measurement Study (LSMS), a national census, or other population-based household surveys
Experience delivering technology for global health or international development programs in low- and middle-income countries
Experience with field data-collection systems for low-connectivity settings (e.g., e, c, ODK), or with offline or edge deployment
Experience working with national statistical offices or ministries of health
Experience leading a stage-gated R&D or innovation portfolio, including a decision to stop a workstream
Experience setting and being held to quantitative acceptance thresholds for an AI or data system
Experience with multi-country deployments where data cannot leave a jurisdiction, and with data privacy and governance for human data, including IRB processes
Experience with cybersecurity practices, security controls, and authorization processes
Publications or conference presentations in AI, survey methods, or global health
Advanced degree in computer science, statistics, demography, public health, or a related field

Professional Skills

Credible with both engineers and executives. Can lead a technical design review in the morning and brief a funder's leadership in the afternoon
Sound judgment under uncertainty. Can tell a workstream that is late from one that isn't going to work, and acts on it
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders, including survey experts and government partners
Strong presentation skills, with the ability to simplify complex topics for business, funder, and program audiences
Works productively and builds relationships at all levels and across cultures, from senior leadership to entry level
Self-motivated. Finds ways to add value without a lot of direct supervision

jobs.description:
Description

Technology Director — Global Health

ICF's Global Health and Development (GHD) line of business, part of the Health, People, and Human Services (HPHS) Group, is seeking a Technology Director
to lead technology modernization efforts across various global health and survey programs. This is a hands-on leadership role. You will own delivery of the program's technology work from end to end. You will also serve as one of its technical leads and architects, designing systems yourself as well as directing the team that builds them. You will bridge ICF's applied AI and software engineers with its survey methodologists, statisticians, field operations staff, and country partners. You will be accountable to the funder for results, including the decision to redirect work that isn't performing and move the funding to work that is.

This position can be remote within the United States, with occasional international travel.

It is contingent upon award of program funding.

Key Responsibilities

Technology Modernization Delivery Leadership

Own delivery of the program's AI innovation portfolio. The workstreams cover automated data-to-report production, natural-language data access, multilingual questionnaire design, field data quality, and new measurement approaches.
Run the stage-gate process. Lead go/no-go reviews, and make and defend decisions to stop workstreams, publish what they learned, and reallocate their funding.
Serve as the principal technical counterpart to the funder. Lead progress reporting and learning reviews. Communicate results candidly, including negative ones.
Manage the innovation portfolio, schedule, and risks with the project manager, including inference and cloud operating costs.
Coordinate across global development programs. Share successes, failures, and methods with technology partners to avoid duplicating work.

Technical Leadership & Architecture

Act as technical lead and architect for a cluster of workstreams. Own their system design, write the design documents, and stay hands-on through prototyping and production.
Define acceptance criteria before the work is judged. With survey experts, set the quantitative quality thresholds each tool must meet, and hold the team (and yourself) to them.
Set architecture and standards across the portfolio: model selection and routing, privacy-preserving design, offline and low-connectivity deployment, and security.
Set engineering practice for the team, including specification-driven development with agentic coding tools, evaluation-first delivery, code review, and testing.
Protect data quality and comparability. Work with survey methodologists so that no innovation breaks the comparability of data across countries and over time.
Oversee responsible AI, data governance, and ethics. Make sure the program meets ICF security standards, IRB requirements, and partner-country data sovereignty expectations.

Team Leadership & Collaboration

Lead and mentor the program's technology team, including applied AI, software, ML, and platform engineers.
Bridge technology and survey expertise. Make sure survey methodologists, statisticians, and field teams shape what gets built, and that engineers understand how surveys work.
Work with national statistical offices and ministries of health, together with ICF's country engagement leads, to design tools that countries want and can run on their own.
Share the program's results openly through public documentation, publications, and presentations at technical and global health conferences.
Contribute to business growth efforts including proactive engagement with potential clients, preparation of white papers, and proposal development.

Minimum Required Experience

Bachelors degree in IT, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical field (or equivalent experience)
Minimum 10 years of professional experience designing and delivering technology solutions, including hands-on architecture of multiple complex systems taken into production
Minimum 5 years leading and mentoring software or data engineering teams to build products or deploy systems

Additional Required Skills And Experience

A track record of architecting and delivering AI/ML or LLM-powered systems in production, and the ability to explain how their quality was measured and where they failed
Experience leading a multi-workstream technology program for a foundation, donor, or government client, with accountability for budget and results
Deep knowledge of system architecture, data pipelines, software development methods, and at least one major cloud platform (e.g., AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud)
Hands-on familiarity with agentic coding tools and specification-driven development, and experience setting how a team uses them
U.S. citizenship is required by federal government contract

Preferred Skills

Working proficiency in French or Portuguese
Background in survey operations or data collection, such as work on or with the Demographic & Health Surveys (DHS) Program, Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS), Living Standards Measurement Study (LSMS), a national census, or other population-based household surveys
Experience delivering technology for global health or international development programs in low- and middle-income countries
Experience with field data-collection systems for low-connectivity settings (e.g., e, c, ODK), or with offline or edge deployment
Experience working with national statistical offices or ministries of health
Experience leading a stage-gated R&D or innovation portfolio, including a decision to stop a workstream
Experience setting and being held to quantitative acceptance thresholds for an AI or data system
Experience with multi-country deployments where data cannot leave a jurisdiction, and with data privacy and governance for human data, including IRB processes
Experience with cybersecurity practices, security controls, and authorization processes
Publications or conference presentations in AI, survey methods, or global health
Advanced degree in computer science, statistics, demography, public health, or a related field

Professional Skills

Credible with both engineers and executives. Can lead a technical design review in the morning and brief a funder's leadership in the afternoon
Sound judgment under uncertainty. Can tell a workstream that is late from one that isn't going to work, and acts on it
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders, including survey experts and government partners
Strong presentation skills, with the ability to simplify complex topics for business, funder, and program audiences
Works productively and builds relationships at all levels and across cultures, from senior leadership to entry level
Self-motivated. Finds ways to add value without a lot of direct supervision

jobs.description:
Duties

Summary

This position is being filled under a stream-lined hiring authority, Title 21 of the United States Code (21 US Code 379d-3a) as amended by the 21st Century Cures Act of 2016, section 3072 and the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2023, Section 3624. The candidate selected for this position will serve under a career or career-conditional appointment and be paid under the provisions of this authority. This position is being recruited based on the Title 21 Pay Table 4, Band G.

Requirements

Qualifications

In order to qualify for the Director, Office of Science and Engineering Laboratories (OSEL) position which falls under the 0801 occupational Series, you must meet the following requirements by 11:59 pm EST on 10/28/2026: The candidate must meet the following qualifications for this Title 21 position: Scientific, Technical, and/or Professional Fields Qualified and Outstanding Candidates a. Qualified applies to all candidates for Cures appointments. The FDA OTS will use the technical qualifications defined below as a baseline for comparing experience levels and other candidate attributes for relevant positions b, Outstanding candidates can be defined by existing outstanding work experience, outstanding performance rating, or both. Basic Requirements A. Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR B. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern(EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1, or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional 1 For more information about EI and EIT registration requirements, please visit the National Society of Professional Engineers website. The FE examination is not administered by the U. S. Office of Personnel Management. For more information please visit: http://www.nspe.org/Licensure/HowtoGetLicensed/index.html.2 registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. 4. Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, maybe accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g.in interdisciplinary positions. Desired Qualifications: Possesses a Ph.D. in the life sciences or an M.D./Ph.D. degree, with advanced research and scientific training relevant to the position. The preferred qualification reflects the depth of research expertise needed to lead multidisciplinary regulatory science programs and address complex scientific and emerging technologies. An M.D. without a Ph.D. is not considered equivalent to the preferred research and scientific background. This position is designated as an SES Equivalent position and is covered under the FDA Title 21 Executive Performance Management System and identified as a public filing position for ethics purposes. While PHS Commissioned Corps Officers cannot hold a Title 21 position during their active service as PHS Officers, we welcome and encourage them to apply-their applications will receive full consideration. Please note that if selected, the Officer will need to end their Commissioned Corps appointment before being placed in the Title 21 position. Supervisory Responsibilities The incumbent is delegated full authority to achieve group goals and objectives through the effective management of available resources. Performance and accomplishments are assessed primarily through work performance indicators, staff discussion, planning sessions, review of individual project outputs, and annual program review. Leads in a proactive, customer-responsive manner consistent with Agency vision and values, effectively communicating program issues to external audiences. Ensures financial and managerial accountability by acting with prudence when executing fiduciary responsibilities. Demonstrates high integrity and adheres to the highest ethical standards of public service. Uses effective business practices including balanced measures of results, values, and invests in each employee; emphasizes empowerment and two-way communication. Takes a leadership role in advocating for and advancing the priorities of the Agency. Serves as a role model for leadership by encouraging teamwork and a collaborative approach. Timely notifies Agency officials of all significant actions and developments, including but not limited to those related to regulatory matters, legislative matters, budget matters, reports, initiatives, and events and ensures subordinate managers do the same. Provides reasonable accommodations needed to best utilize qualified people with disabilities. Organizational Management: Manages the Office of Science and Engineering Laboratories (OSEL) within CDRH Program Management: Runs a multidisciplinary regulatory science program in the Center encompassing multiple laboratories and scientific disciplines. Directs and evaluates activities addressing scientific and technical questions relevant to medical devices and radiation-emitting products, including test methods, biocompatibility, biological testing, in vitro/in vivo evaluation, computational modeling, and reference materials. Resource Management: Monitors and reports on resources needed to lead strategic resource planning for OSEL and its multidisciplinary regulatory science programs. Establishes annual and multi-year objectives, determines program priorities, and allocates resources across OSEL's scientific programs. Human Capital Management: Identifies employee competencies necessary to meet OSEL's organizational capabilities goals across its multidisciplinary scientific workforce. Designs competency frameworks and workforce architecture to ensure OSEL maintains the scientific capabilities needed for current and emerging regulatory science challenges.

Become a part of the Department that touches the lives of every American. At the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) you can give back to your community, state, and country, by making a difference in the lives of Americans everywhere! HHS is the principal agency for protecting the health of citizens. Join HHS and help to make our world healthier, safer, and better for all Americans. The position is located in the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH), Office of Science and Engineering Laboratories (OSEL). CDRH assures that patients and providers have timely and continued access to safe, effective, and high-quality medical devices and safe radiation-emitting products.

jobs.title: VP of Engineering
jobs.description:
Our Mission and Vision

Unlearn exists to transform clinical development by making every trial smarter. We harness data, AI, and digital twins to enable faster, more robust studies that bring life-saving treatments to patients faster. This mission drives everything we do as we partner with biopharmaceutical companies to redesign how clinical trials are planned, run, and analyzed.

We are defining the future of clinical development with unmatched scientific credibility, replacing uncertainty with AI-powered precision so decisions are clearer and trials are stronger. We don’t just disrupt the pharmaceutical industry, we create lasting change.

We believe AI will define the future of medicine, and we are committed to building that future responsibly, rigorously, and in close collaboration with our partners in clinical development.

About Our Team

We come from a variety of backgrounds ranging from machine learning to marketing—but regardless of where we come from, Unlearners share some common traits:

Unlearners are ambitious; we aren’t intimidated by big, challenging goals.
Unlearners are disciplined experimenters; we break down our big goals into smaller chunks and meet as often as necessary to track our velocity and iterate quickly.
Unlearners are gritty; we never give up, setbacks just make us try harder.
Unlearners are receptive to new ideas; in fact, we hate being stuck with the status quo
Unlearners are storytellers; sharing information with each other and with the world is super important, too important to be boring. And, last but not least,
Unlearners are team-oriented; we put the mission first, the company second, the team third, and individuals last.

Headquartered in San Francisco, Unlearn was founded in 2017 by a team of world-class machine learning scientists. We have raised venture capital from top tier investors such as Altimeter, Insight Partners, Radical Ventures, 8VC, DCVC, and DCVC Bio, and completed our $50 million Series C in January 2024.

If our purpose and culture resonate with you, we invite you to apply.

Your Role

Leading Pharma and Biotech companies trust Unlearn to deliver scientifically rigorous work using digital twins on studies where the stakes are high and the timelines are real. A digital twin of a patient is a comprehensive prediction of expected outcomes under a defined standard of care, made by a machine learning model built using our proprietary technology. Working at scale across the industry requires a strong engineering foundation built around data, models, and AI in a regulated, compliance-heavy environment.

As the VP of Engineering, you will lead our engineering function, an organization of engineers spanning core engineering, applications, ML/AI Ops, and infrastructure. The team includes engineers across experience levels, anchored by strong senior technical leaders. Engineering plays a critical role in our ability to deliver AI technology through models, applications, and agentic systems, and this role will ensure the potential of AI systems are realized across that technical stack.

This is an execution-focused leadership role, focused on the core engineering systems, software applications, infrastructure, and forward deployment that drive AI-heavy, tech-enabled services. You will work with your teams on scoping and delivery, and lead an engineering organization known for shipping what it commits to. You will partner closely with Product, Delivery, and R&D teams to understand requirements, integrate engineering with our customer delivery teams, and build the platform and tools they use to do their best work.

Just as importantly, you will connect engineering to the company's direction, understanding company strategy, translating it into a concrete engineering roadmap that integrates a workflow across data, modeling, applications, compliance, and security, and holding the team accountable for delivering to that roadmap on timeframes that match company objectives. You will work as a member of the leadership team, maintaining consistent communication and clear expectations in both directions, so that leadership always knows where engineering stands, and engineering always knows why its work matters.

Responsibilities

Lead Unlearn's engineering function across technical disciplines, owning the quality, reliability, compliance, and security of the systems that power our work. Ensure AI tools and systems are used heavily for efficiency and impact.
Drive execution: define projects, partner with teams on scoping and estimation, and run delivery practices that turn commitments into shipped work. Partner with Product, R&D, and Delivery leadership to understand requirements, shape technical approaches, and deliver on value for customers.
Translate company strategy to sequence and prioritize work so that engineering output directly advances company objectives, and hold teams accountable for delivering to that roadmap on the timeframes the business requires.
Operate as a member of the leadership team: report clearly and consistently on engineering progress, capacity, and risk; maintain aligned expectations between leadership and the engineering team; and communicate priorities and context down into the organization.
Establish an AI-centric engineering culture, one that scales the impact of the organization and likewise equips team members with strong, modern toolsets to help them grow and succeed in their careers at and beyond Unlearn.
Own hiring and team design for engineering, deliberately growing the organization aligned with company needs.

Requirements

10+ years in software engineering with significant experience leading engineering organizations at the Senior Director or VP level, including managing managers and senior technical leaders across multiple engineering disciplines.
A track record of strong execution in highly collaborative and cross-functional environments where engineering has delivered on timelines that mattered to the business.
Experience leading across the stack: infrastructure/DevOps, backend or platform engineering, and application/front-end development, with experience in regulated environments where compliance is a key factor on system design.
Demonstrated ability to translate company strategy into an engineering roadmap, communicate the "why" behind priorities, and hold teams accountable for delivering against commitments.
Experience partnering closely with Product, R&D, and customer-facing delivery teams; you have built internal tools and platforms that made technical teams measurably more effective.
Experience in growth-stage or early-stage companies where you built engineering processes and delivery discipline in small teams while shipping. Experience in life sciences, healthcare, or another regulated, data-intensive domain is a plus.

Benefits & Perks

The following benefits and perks are for full time roles only.

Meaningful equity participation
100% company-covered medical, dental, & vision insurance plans
401k plan with matching
Flexible PTO plus company holidays
Annual company-wide break December 24 through January 1
Commuter benefits
Paid Parental Leave

Unlearn is an equal opportunity employer.

At Unlearn, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace, because inclusion and diversity are essential to achieving our mission. If you’re excited about this role, and your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply nevertheless.
